title: ENG-205 Sir Gawain Part 2 — 4 Main Ideas
subject: ENG-205

cards.term: Part 2 summary: where things stand
cards.def: Gawain is spending the last days before New Year at Bertilak's castle near the Green Chapel, dreading the return blow he must take on New Year's Day and bound by his promise to trade each evening whatever he gains indoors for whatever Bertilak wins hunting.

cards.term: Part 2 summary: three days of hunts and temptations
cards.def: On three mornings Bertilak hunts in the woods while Lady Bertilak slips into Gawain's bedroom to seduce him, and Gawain, trying to stay both courteous and chaste, lets her give him only kisses, which he hands over to Bertilak each night.

cards.term: Part 2 summary: the green girdle
cards.def: On the third morning Gawain accepts Lady Bertilak's green silk girdle because she says it protects its wearer from any blow, promises to hide it from her husband, and that night gives Bertilak only three kisses, breaking the bargain just before he leaves for the Green Chapel.

cards.term: The three hunts and the three temptations
cards.def: Fitt III alternates outdoor hunts with indoor temptations in order, the deer hunt with the first bedroom visit, the boar hunt with the second, and the fox hunt with the third, and each day ends with an exchange of winnings at the castle.

cards.term: Lady Bertilak's three bedroom visits
cards.def: On the first morning Lady Bertilak offers herself and wins a kiss by doubting Gawain's courtesy, on the second she begs him to teach her about love, and on the third she presses for his love and a keepsake until he takes her girdle.

cards.term: The three evening exchanges of winnings
cards.def: Each evening Bertilak gives Gawain his kill, a pile of deer, then a boar, then a fox pelt, and Gawain gives back his gains as kisses, one, then two, then three, while secretly keeping the girdle on the last night.

cards.term: Why Gawain accepts the green girdle
cards.def: Gawain refuses Lady Bertilak's gold ring and at first her girdle, but accepts the girdle once she claims no one can slay its wearer, because he thinks it might save him from the axe at the Green Chapel.

cards.term: How Gawain breaks the bargain
cards.def: By promising Lady Bertilak to keep the girdle secret and giving Bertilak only three kisses, Gawain keeps his chastity and courtesy but fails the exchange of winnings, which is his test of trouthe.

cards.term: How Bertilak's first hunt begins
cards.def: At dawn on the first day, after mass and a quick meal, Bertilak rides out with about a hundred hunters and their hounds to the sound of bugles, starting the deer hunt that runs alongside Gawain's first temptation.

cards.term: How Lady Bertilak enters Gawain's room on the first morning
cards.def: While Bertilak hunts, Lady Bertilak quietly enters Gawain's bedroom and sits on his bed while he pretends to sleep, and when he finally wakes and crosses himself she laughs that he is "tricked and trapped."

cards.term: How Gawain handles Lady Bertilak's first-morning offer
cards.def: When Lady Bertilak, with her husband away and the door bolted, offers herself to Gawain, he answers with modest compliments and vows to be her servant, countering her every move "case by case."

cards.term: Why Gawain stays cool with Lady Bertilak
cards.def: On the first morning Gawain stays gracious but on guard with Lady Bertilak because his mind is on the strike he must receive at the Green Chapel.

cards.term: How the first kiss happens
cards.def: As she leaves on the first morning, Lady Bertilak says the real Gawain would never stay so long with a lady without claiming a kiss, so Gawain agrees to kiss at her command and she kisses him.

cards.term: What happens to the deer after the first hunt
cards.def: At the end of the first day Bertilak's hunters ritually butcher, or "dress," the deer, share out portions to every man and feed the hounds, then carry the meat home to the castle.

cards.term: The first evening exchange
cards.def: Bertilak gives Gawain the venison, Gawain repays him with one kiss, and when Bertilak asks where Gawain won it Gawain replies that wasn't part of their pact, so they renew the deal for the next day.

cards.term: How Bertilak kills the boar on the second day
cards.def: The huge old boar wounds hounds and men and turns away arrows until Bertilak wades into the stream alone and kills it with his sword in the water.

cards.term: Lady Bertilak's second-morning complaint
cards.def: On the second morning Lady Bertilak reminds Gawain of yesterday's lesson about kissing and asks why a famous knight, whose chivalry should mean loyalty in love, has not said one word about love to her.

cards.term: How Gawain answers Lady Bertilak's request to teach love
cards.def: Gawain tells Lady Bertilak it would be presumptuous to explain love to a lady more skilled in it than he, but promises to serve her, so she leaves after two kisses with no sin on either side.

cards.term: The second evening exchange
cards.def: Bertilak gives Gawain the boar, and Gawain repays him with two kisses, so Bertilak swears by Saint Giles that Gawain is the best man he knows.

cards.term: Why Gawain stays a third day
cards.def: When Gawain asks to leave so he can reach the Green Chapel in time, Bertilak swears Gawain will get there before dawn on New Year's Day and persuades him to play the game one more day.

cards.term: How the fox hunt runs on the third day
cards.def: On the frosty third morning the hounds chase a crafty fox, Reynard, who doubles back and hides all day until Bertilak finally takes it from the hounds and it is skinned.

cards.term: Why the third morning is the most dangerous
cards.def: On the third morning Lady Bertilak comes in a revealing gown while Gawain is dreaming of the death blow, and he feels real passion, so he must either accept her love or rudely refuse it.

cards.term: Gawain's answer to Lady Bertilak about another lady
cards.def: When Lady Bertilak says Gawain must already love another lady, Gawain swears to her by Saint John there is no other, which she calls the worst answer of all before asking him for a keepsake such as a glove.

cards.term: How Lady Bertilak offers the ring and the girdle
cards.def: When Gawain says he has nothing fine enough to give, Lady Bertilak offers him a rich gold ring, which he refuses because he has nothing to give in return, and then her green silk girdle, which he also refuses at first.

cards.term: The secrecy promise and the third kiss
cards.def: Once Gawain accepts the girdle, Lady Bertilak begs him not to tell her husband about it, Gawain agrees, and she gives him a third kiss and leaves.

cards.term: What Gawain does after taking the girdle
cards.def: Gawain hides the "love-lace" from all eyes, confesses his sins to the castle priest, who declares him clean enough for Doomsday, and is merrier that evening than ever before.

cards.term: The third evening's incomplete exchange
cards.def: Gawain greets Bertilak first with three kisses, while Bertilak apologizes that he has only a "foul-stinking fox" to offer, and the girdle is never mentioned.

cards.term: How the hunt-temptation structure tests trouthe
cards.def: Each day's more cunning quarry, deer, then boar, then fox, mirrors a sharper bedroom test, until the fox-day secrecy breaks the exchange of winnings even though Gawain's courtesy and chastity largely hold.

cards.term: The conflict between courtesy and loyalty in the bedroom
cards.def: On the third morning Gawain must avoid being rude to Lady Bertilak while also guarding his soul from sin and avoiding being counted a betrayer by his host, showing how courtly manners and loyalty to a lord pull against each other.

cards.term: Why keeping the girdle is a lapse in trouthe
cards.def: Gawain had pledged to trade everything he gained at the castle, yet he holds back the girdle because he hopes it will save his life, so his word fails at the one point where his own survival is at stake.
